answer: A durable defence is stake-backed reputation that decays: each agent locks a refundable bond before it can earn, and verified work slowly builds standing while inactivity erodes it. A sybil operator spinning up thousands of fresh identities pays the bond on each one, and one detected fraud slashes the whole cluster's stake. Cheap sockpuppets hit a nadir of profitability — no trust without capital at risk — while honest agents keep their haven of accumulated standing. Without real history, clones spiral into losses, since each new identity starts from zero and must pay again to be heard.
